title: Djokovic Rallies and Sabalenka Wins at China Open
summary:
Novak Djokovic came back from a set down to win at the China Open in Beijing. The 39-year-old Serb beat China's Bu Yunchaokete 4-6, 7-6 (7-2), 6-2 in two hours and 52 minutes.

Djokovic has won the tournament six times and has won all 31 matches he has played in Beijing. Bu made this match difficult for him. In the second set, Djokovic lost a service game after taking a lead and needed a medical timeout. He received a time violation while trying to regain his breath between points. He also consulted a trainer, as he had during his first-round win over Nuno Borges.

Djokovic then won the tie-break 7-2. In the deciding set, he won four games in a row and finished the match with a backhand winner. He will face either Germany's Alexander Zverev or China's Shang Juncheng on Saturday for a place in the quarter-finals.

In the women's event, world number two Aryna Sabalenka began with a 6-1, 6-3 victory over Mexico's Renata Zarazua. Sabalenka hit 11 aces and did not face a break point. The match lasted 63 minutes.

It was her first match since losing her world number one ranking and her US Open title to Elena Rybakina in September. Sabalenka is seeking her first title since March, when she won Indian Wells and the Miami Open back-to-back.

Asked about being self-critical, Sabalenka explained that expecting more from herself sometimes helps her move forward, but sometimes drains her energy. She said she is trying to be easier on herself.

Sabalenka will next face Czech 20-year-old Nikola Bartunkova, who came close to beating her at the Berlin Open in June. Rybakina, the top seed, begins her tournament on Saturday.

Elsewhere, Katie Boulter lost to Karolina Muchova. Mirra Andreeva recovered from losing the first set to beat Yuan Yue 3-6, 6-0, 6-0. Daniil Medvedev hit 12 aces to beat Pablo Carreno Busta 6-4, 6-2. British pair Julian Cash and Lloyd Glasspool beat Andrey Rublev and Karen Khachanov in doubles.
why_it_matters: The article follows two players advancing at the China Open. Djokovic's comeback illustrates how a match can change after the first set, while Sabalenka explains the mixed effects of demanding more from herself.
